record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: In the base-10 consecutive concatenation sequence 1, 12, 123, 1234, 12345, ... obtained by writing the positive integers in order without separators, how many terms are prime, and what happens to the corresponding prime-counting question when the same construction is carried out in an arbitrary numeration base B?

evidence.quote: How many primes are there among these numbers?  In general form, the Consecutive Sequence is considered in an arbitrary numeration base B.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer base $B \geq 2$, define the consecutive concatenation sequence $(S_n^{(B)})_{n\geq 1}$ as follows: write the positive integers $1, 2, 3, \dots, n$ in their standard base-$B$ representations (without leading zeros) and concatenate these digit strings in order; let $S_n^{(B)}$ be the integer whose base-$B$ representation is this concatenation. For example, in base $B=10$ one obtains $S_1=1$, $S_2=12$, $S_3=123$, $S_4=1234$, $S_5=12345$, $S_{10}=12345678910$, and so on.

(a) Determine the number of indices $n \geq 1$ for which $S_n^{(10)}$ is a prime number; in particular, decide whether the set $\{n : S_n^{(10)} \text{ is prime}\}$ is empty, finite and nonempty, or infinite.

(b) More generally, for an arbitrary integer base $B \geq 2$, determine (or characterize) the cardinality of the set $\{n \geq 1 : S_n^{(B)} \text{ is prime}\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The base-10 case is the well-known Smarandache–Wellin-style "consecutive concatenation" sequence (OEIS A007908). No prime term is known: extensive searches have ruled out primes for n up to at least the hundreds of thousands, but no proof exists that the sequence contains no primes or only finitely many. The general base-B version is likewise unresolved. The problem is widely cited as open in number-theoretic surveys and the OEIS entry.

status_evidence.title: Consecutive Number Sequences -- MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: No prime Smarandache numbers Sm(n) exist for n<=344869 (Great Smarandache PRPrime search).
status_evidence.claim: It is unknown whether any term of the base-10 consecutive concatenation sequence is prime; large searches have found none.

status_evidence.title: A007908 / A019518 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: Concatenation of the first n positive integers. It is an open problem whether any term is prime.
status_evidence.claim: OEIS records the primality question as open.
